cases.note: A quantitative position scale defaults to zero, so the axis starts at 0 even though the data spans 3 to 7.
`zero: false` fits the domain to the data extent, so the axis starts at 3 and the baseline moves.
`nice: true` rounds the authored 0 to 17 domain outward to whole ticks, so the axis end exceeds the data maximum.
`nice: false` keeps the authored 0 to 17 domain verbatim, so the axis end is a fractional tick position.
Disabling zero and enabling nice act independently: the domain fits the data and is then rounded outward.
A log scale places decades evenly and does not accept a zero anchor, so the axis starts at the first decade above 3.
